newsitem.title: HONG KONG: China zinc smelter sees high prices good for export.
newsitem.headline: China zinc smelter sees high prices good for export.

text.p: China's Zhuzhou smelter, one of the country's largest for lead and zinc, says high zinc prices at the London Metal Exchange (LME) made it lucrative to buy old zinc for reprocessing and export.
"The LME price above $1,200 is good enough to profit from tolling between China's national warehouses and the export market," a Zhuzhou smelter source told Reuters on Tuesday.
"We buy old material stored in national (state) warehouses at cheaper prices and process it again and export it to other markets."

Old zinc from state warehouses was available at 8,000-9,000 yuan ($1,060-$1,084) per tonne, compared with the domestic Chinese market price of about 10,000 yuan ($1,208) per tonne for 99.99 percent specifications, the source said.
"We can continue doing this till the LME price drops," he said.
The smelter also planned to export a "large quantity" of zinc to Singapore LME warehouses in March since the prices were so favourable, the source said.
LME zinc touched a 4-1/2 year high of $1,266 per tonne on Friday before closing a touch lower at $1,254 per tonne.
Zhuzhou lead and zinc smelter plans to export about half of the zinc it produces in 1997, another company official said.
"We will produce about 210,000 tonnes of zinc and export around half of that this year," said Shu Yuzhang, director of the smelter's technical development department.
Most of the smelter's exports between January and March went to Japan, Shu told Reuters while attending a week-long China non-ferrous metals fair being held in Hong Kong.
The smelter produced 170,000 tonnes of zinc in 1996.
Domestic zinc prices were slowly rising, with the market price rising to more than 10,000 yuan per tonne from about 9,000 yuan per tonne last year, Shu said.
"Last year, 1996, was a very difficult year for us," Shu said, noting that domestic zinc prices were weak, as were international prices.
